transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-09-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM), Ibrahim Patel (Redwood AE); Nina Kapoor (Verdant Head of ML), Liam O'Reilly (Infra Lead), Jae Park (Security Architect), Sofia Morales (Product Ops)

Auto-generated summary: Verdant needs an uplift in reserved capacity for Q4 and wants to scope an EU on-prem node for regulatory workloads. Action: Redwood to provide quote + runbench plan.

[00:00] Samantha Lee: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — I'll kick off. Um, quick check that folks can hear me?
[00:07] Nina Kapoor: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:09] Liam O'Reilly: All good here.
[00:11] Samantha Lee: Great. Today's agenda is quick renewal sync, go over the capacity ask for Q4, and then dig into the EU on-prem extension scope that Jae requested. Diego will cover performance details, and Maya will talk through the support/SLAs.
[00:27] Diego Ramos: Hey, hi. So on the capacity piece, Verdant mentioned earlier in email that you're looking to bump from 4 to 12 reserved GPU slots for inference — is that still the target? And are we thinking full-time reserved or a mix reserved + burstable?
[00:40] Nina Kapoor: That's right. We've been trending up — our inference traffic for product recommendations spiked after the last release. Main ask is predictable throughput for peak hours, so reserved is preferred but we'd like some burst headroom. Budget will allow some mix but we want hard SLOs.
[00:55] Jae Park: We also need the EU on-prem for a subset of PII workloads; that can't leave our data center. So the plan is: replicate inference only for those endpoints, rest stays on hosted. Security wise we need KMS integration and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Do you support HSM-backed keys?
[01:12] Diego Ramos: Yes, we have KMS hooks; HSM integrations depend on the deployment model but for Private (on-prem) we support customer-managed KMS and can integrate with HSM-backed vaults. I should mention sometimes the docs call out KV cache as "K V cash" in transcripts, sorry — but yes, KV cache and prefix caching are supported.
[01:30] Liam O'Reilly: Good. For the on-prem box, we're thinking a 4-GPU rack initially, but we'd like a recommendation whether that matches 12 reserved slots in hosted. Do you map slots to GPUs linearly?
[01:44] Diego Ramos: It's not strictly 1:1, depends on model, token lengths, batching. For our default GPT-style L40 family, roughly 3–4 reserved slots per A40-class GPU for sustained throughput, assuming 2–4k token windows. But if you're running longer contexts or larger batch sizes, that number changes. We can run a sizing test.
[02:02] Sofia Morales: When you say "sizing test" — what does that look like operationally? We need to align timelines for procurement.
[02:09] Diego Ramos: We'll run a two-part benchmark: synthetic throughput to measure tokens/sec under different batching configs, and a realistic replay with your payloads to measure latency P50/P95. We'll also do cold-start tests for scale-up and warm-cache steady state. Should take about 6–8 hours of wall time across teams.
[02:25] Nina Kapoor: Can we prioritize P95 latency? Our SLAs for customer-facing recs are strict.
[02:30] Maya Chen: On SLAs, we can offer reserved capacity with a 99.9% uptime SLO for Dedicated; for Private deployments we provide an operational rubric plus a handoff runbook. Contractually, Enterprise add-ons include higher retention for traces and extended support hours.
[02:46] Jae Park: About compliance: we've got to verify SOC 2 coverage for any hosted data, plus we need full audit logs for the on-prem. What about encryption in transit and at rest? Also data residency — logs must stay in EU for those workloads.
[02:59] Diego Ramos: Encryption in transit is standard TLS. At rest, for hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer keys via KMS. For Private, all storage is under your control and we can plug into your HSM. Audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM over syslog or S3 endpoints hosted in your environment.
[03:15] Liam O'Reilly: For network, likely we'll do VPC peering for hosted-to-onprem lanes — or maybe it's V P C peering? — anyway, do you support site-to-site VPN and VPC peering?
[03:24] Ibrahim Patel: Yes, we support both. For Private we do customer-managed networking and can handle either scenario. We'll need to agree NAT rules and allowed ports. Our security docs list the ports; Diego will share the minimal rules.
[03:38] Diego Ramos: I'll send the network diagram and the port list. Also want to call out a tradeoff: if you want sub-10ms local inference in EU, on-prem is the best; if 20–50ms is acceptable, Dedicated in region with sessions pinned to EU edge might suffice and is cheaper operationally.
[03:57] Nina Kapoor: Hm, target is P95 < 60ms for recommendation render. Ideally <40 but we'll take 60. Cost is a factor but data residency and SLA push us to on-prem for the sensitive flows.
[04:10] Jae Park: Another question: how do you handle rollouts and model version pinning for on-prem vs hosted? We can't have an automatic push that risks data leaks.
[04:20] Diego Ramos: Good point. For Private, the control plane can be configured read-only for model updates; you can pin versions and we support canary style deployments with manual approval. We also support checksum verification on model artifacts.
[04:33] Sofia Morales: Contract timing — we have a license renewal in early November. What's the minimum lead time to provision the on-prem cluster?
[04:40] Samantha Lee: Typical lead time for provisioning hardware + integration is 6–8 weeks once orders and security docs are in place. If you want us to meet November, we'd need to lock commitments by late September.
[04:52] Nina Kapoor: OK that tracks. We'll aim to get the internal approvals this week.
[04:56] Diego Ramos: For benchmarks, we prefer you share a small representative dataset to replay; privacy redacts are fine. We'll also kick off a short reference harness that runs in your environment so we measure the on-prem network overhead.
[05:09] Liam O'Reilly: About maintenance windows — how disruptive are kernel upgrades or Redwood runtime restarts? We need to schedule around daily churn windows.
[05:18] Diego Ramos: Runtime upgrades are rolling and typically have no impact if you use the built-in rolling update strategy; cache warm-up is the tricky bit — you may see a slightly higher latency spike during the initial ramp after a major rollout. We can use blue/green or canary to mitigate.
[05:32] Jae Park: On the security checklist, can you confirm you provide signed attestations for images and a vulnerability scan report prior to handoff?
[05:40] Maya Chen: Yes, we can provide SBOM and vulnerability scan outputs for the runtime images along with attestations. For Private installs we can run an on-site verification or a remote attestation session.
[05:51] Nina Kapoor: Pricing-wise, what's the delta between dedicated reserved and a private on-prem license? Ballpark numbers are fine for now.
[05:57] Samantha Lee: Ballpark: a dedicated reserved pool with 12 slots will be Xk/month (we'll send exact numbers). Private has a platform fee plus a per-GPU support/ops charge and an installation fee; it ends up higher upfront but lower variable usage cost. We'll put these line items in the updated quote.
[06:14] Sofia Morales: Can you include optional burstable credits in that quote? We need a safety valve during marketing spikes.
[06:19] Samantha Lee: Yes, burst packages and emergency credits are standard add-ons; we'll include them.
[06:22] Nina Kapoor: On SLAs, will a private deployment get the same SLA we expect for Dedicated?
[06:27] Maya Chen: Private deployments don't have a vendor-managed uptime SLA by default because it's customer-hosted, but we provide an SLA for the control plane and an operational runbook with guaranteed response times for support tiers. For enterprise contracts we can negotiate extended support commitments.
[06:42] Liam O'Reilly: One operational nit: how do you handle model telemetry and cost attribution? We need per-route token accounting and attribution so finance can report on unit costs.
[06:51] Diego Ramos: We emit per-request telemetry, token counts, model version, and route tags. In Private, we can stream that telemetry to an internal collector or keep a local retention. Billing is flexible — we can generate usage reports compatible with your chargeback pipeline.
[07:07] Nina Kapoor: Okay. I'd like to propose a pilot: provision a 4-GPU on-prem node in EU, run your bench suite against our replay, validate P95 < 60ms, and if green we'll sign an extension that shifts 6 of the 12 reserved hosted slots into on-prem. Thoughts?
[07:21] Diego Ramos: Sounds reasonable. The pilot would need: hardware provisioning on your side, a short network setup, and the replay artifacts. We'll provide the runbook and assist with the initial deployment.
[07:33] Jae Park: We'll want a security run-through during the pilot — vulnerability scans, key exchange, and audit log integration.
[07:40] Maya Chen: We'll include a security checklist item in the runbook.
[07:45] Samantha Lee: Great. Let's recap action items right now so nothing falls through.
[07:49] Samantha Lee: Diego to send benchmark plan and port list; Diego to lead the runbook session (owner: Diego).
[07:55] Samantha Lee: Samantha to update the pricing and include burst credits and private platform fees and send the formal quote.
[08:02] Samantha Lee: Jae to share the security/Qs doc and the network diagram.
[08:06] Nina Kapoor: We'll target sending the network diagram and compliance questions by 2027-09-21.
[08:12] Diego Ramos: I'll set up a 2-hour runbook workshop for next Tuesday 2027-09-21 or the 22nd — I'll send a Doodle.
[08:19] Liam O'Reilly: Doodle is good. Also, can we get a sample SLO for Dedicated vs Private in writing so we can show procurement?
[08:26] Maya Chen: Yep I'll attach the SLO matrix and the differences in the quote.
[08:30] Samantha Lee: Any other blockers?
[08:33] Sofia Morales: Not from product ops. Procurement will need the formal quote and SLOs.
[08:37] Nina Kapoor: Nothing else. Thanks everyone.
[08:39] Samantha Lee: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the quote and the runbook plan.

Recap / Next steps (auto):
- Redwood to provide the updated committed capacity quote with private add-on and burst credits included.
- SE to prepare benchmark/runbook and schedule 2-hour workshop week of 2027-09-21.

- Action owners assigned and deadlines recorded.

End of transcript.
